prompt: Where does the shell get a course's site name from?

options.text: The first lesson's title
The "name" field in course.json
A constant in the shell's source code
The repository description on GitHub

explanation: The shell holds no course-specific text. Name, colours and home page copy all come from course.json.

prompt: A course.json sets only "brand": { "color": "#0D9488" }. What happens to the lighter and darker brand shades?

options.text: Validation fails until all eleven shades are listed
The shell falls back to its own default colours
The shell derives the scale, the gradient and the logo from that one colour
The site is drawn in black and white

explanation: One colour is enough. An exact scale and gradient are optional, for a course that needs precise brand colours.

prompt: Which of these are set per course in course.json? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The kinds a lesson can be
The languages that code blocks may use
The layout of the lesson page
The home page headline

explanation: Kinds, code languages and home page copy belong to the course. Layout belongs to the shell and is the same everywhere.

prompt: Which section of a bite must contain exactly three bullets?
explanation: Remember always lists exactly three takeaways. The validator counts them.

prompt: Match each shape of information to the visual that fits it.

pairs.left: Things compared on the same properties

explanation: Choose the visual from the shape of the information, not out of habit.

prompt: A draft bite comes out at seven minutes. What should you do?

options.text: Type a shorter reading time into the front-matter
Split it into two bites and link them as related
Move the extra text into a sixth section
Remove the example to save space

explanation: Reading time is computed, never typed, and the limit is five minutes. A longer bite is two ideas.

prompt: Put the steps of publishing a change to a course in order.

items.text: Edit a lesson while the dev preview is running
The workflow checks out the shell, validates and builds
GitHub Pages serves the new site

explanation: Preview and validate locally, then push. The workflow repeats the strict check before it builds and deploys.

prompt: The shared interface was improved in the shell repository. When does an existing course get the change?

options.text: Immediately, without any deploy
Never, unless the interface code is copied into the course
The next time the course's deploy workflow runs
Only after its course.json is rewritten

explanation: Each deploy builds the course with the latest shell, so a push or a manual workflow run picks the change up.
